decisions.decision: Reuse config_images_locations with two new scopes, visual_part and wip_part, for part pictures
decisions.why: The table already carries a scope, an item key, a relative path, an actor and a timestamp, and four mechanisms are built on it: the read and write services, the storage service with its archive, the picture editor base and the part-pictures entitlement. The existing unique key already enforces one picture per scope and key.
decisions.rejected: A dedicated config_part_pictures table, which would duplicate all four mechanisms and drift from them

decisions.decision: Add config_images_locations_history for the who, when and what-was-replaced record
decisions.why: The picture row says who touched it last and holds no previous value, so it cannot answer FR-027 for a second replacement. A history table is the auditability shape the schema rules prescribe, and the row is written in the same transaction as the change it records.
decisions.rejected: A previous_image_path column, which holds one step and loses each earlier actor and time

decisions.decision: Take the owner layout literally: Waitlist, Visual and WIP collections; family folders MMC, MMF, FGT and Categorized Parts; the three existing scope names kept verbatim as the kind folders inside Waitlist
decisions.why: Keeping request_item, request_category and work_center verbatim makes the move an insertion of one folder level rather than a rename of three, and the per-kind folders settle the case-only collision between the item other and the category Other without renaming either.
decisions.rejected: Category-named family folders, which contradict the dictated layout and make Component both a category and the catch-all

decisions.decision: Leave the job per-part picture value unread (OQ-5)
decisions.why: It is always empty and copied forward on every save, so giving it a meaning would create a second answer for one part, which is how a card and a page end up disagreeing.
decisions.rejected: Adopting it as a per-job override, which the specification does not ask for

decisions.decision: The store value wins the folder disagreement and the storage screen shows it rather than hiding it (OQ-3)
decisions.why: That is the cascade ImageStorageConfigurationResolver already implements, and a screen that resolved differently from every reader would be worse than the disagreement it fixes.
decisions.rejected: Letting appsettings.json win, which would let one machine read a share no other machine reads

decisions.decision: The part-number limit is 190 characters, the width of scope_item_id (OQ-4)
decisions.why: It is the only ceiling this application can state without inventing one. Measuring the longest number in use needs a live Infor Visual read this planning step does not have, and a refusal at 190 is a refusal at a number no real part has reached.
decisions.rejected: The legacy 260-character path limit, which the store would fail before reaching, with a worse message

decisions.decision: The two part collections leave the startup mirror and are copied on first draw by a new store
decisions.why: FR-030 asks for exactly this. ImageCacheSyncService mirrors whole trees at startup, which is right for hundreds of item, work-centre, category and dunnage pictures and wrong for a part count copied onto every machine at every start. The copy rule is the same rule with a different trigger.
decisions.rejected: Mirroring everything at startup, which leaves the requirement unsatisfied at real cost

decisions.decision: One archive retention setting, image_storage.archive_keep_days, defaulting to ninety days, cleaned up with the startup cache step
decisions.why: The key already exists and is already read through the resolver, so the work is the default, the screen and the cleanup. One period for the one archive folder, because two periods over one folder is how a cleanup removes something a reader expects to find.
decisions.rejected: A second setting for part pictures only, which is two answers over one folder

decisions.decision: The storage folders and the picture cache are gated on permission.settings.storage_paths, not on the picture entitlement
decisions.why: FR-025 widens the picture entitlement to Setup Lead and Plant Manager while FR-017 keeps the folders on IT Department and Developer. The cache panel sits on the picture entitlement today only because the two had the same members; after the widening a Setup Lead could point this machine picture cache at any folder.
decisions.rejected: Leaving the cache panel where it is and accepting the widening

decisions.decision: The missing-picture list covers the parts this application can name: the WIP inventory parts and the Visual parts the existing read shapes return, minus the pictured rows, with a typed part number always settable
decisions.why: FR-001 defines the universe that way. A complete Visual catalogue would need a read shape this application does not have, over an external system it only reads through the shapes it has, and the typed path is what makes the gap safe: nothing is unpicturable, only unlisted.
decisions.rejected: A cross-database join between mtm_waitlist and mtm_wip_application_winforms, which crosses the store boundary and still does not reach Visual

decisions.decision: The export uses Microsoft.Windows.Storage.Pickers.FileSavePicker with the app window identity
decisions.why: It is the Windows App SDK save picker for a desktop app, this project references Windows App SDK 2.3.1, and the usage was checked against Microsoft Learn rather than recalled.
decisions.rejected: Windows.Storage.Pickers.FileSavePicker, which needs a separate InitializeWithWindow call with the window handle

decisions.decision: The reader resolves both the pre-move and the post-move layout, and the move ships as a run-once tool plus a paired path rewrite
decisions.why: FR-036 promises no picture is left unresolvable. Files and rows move at different moments and the sequence can be interrupted, so tolerance in the reader makes the promise unconditional, and a reviewed run-once step is what the schema rules require instead of a mutation on startup.
decisions.rejected: A one-way rewrite with a maintenance window, whose interruption leaves pictures unresolvable

decisions.decision: A file-name collision is refused by a case-insensitive comparison scoped to one system and one family folder
decisions.why: FR-007 asks for the refusal and for it to name the holder, and the edge case asks the case-only collision to be refused rather than silently overwritten, because the file system is not case-sensitive. Two systems and the three kinds already live in different folders, so scoping to one folder is what the layout promises.
decisions.rejected: Appending a disambiguating suffix, which breaks the file-drop path that depends on the name a person already knows

decisions.decision: One shared card template using Min and Max bounds rather than a fixed tile
decisions.why: FR-021 converts four lists and FR-023 requires each to draw the placeholder rather than an empty tile, so one template with one picture rule keeps four lists from answering the same question four ways. Fixed pixel bounds are what the constitution rules out for a layout-critical container.
decisions.rejected: Copying the existing fixed 150 by 170 tile into each converted list

decisions.decision: The picture change record is written by an AFTER INSERT trigger and a guarded AFTER UPDATE trigger, declared in the two write procedures own create.sql files. Reason: MySQL reports a CALL affected-row count as the count of the last statement executed inside the procedure, so a body ending in COMMIT would report 0 and the existing ImageOverrideWriteService treats anything but 1 as a database error. A trigger leaves both procedures byte-identical, keeps their signature and their answer unchanged, and writes the history row inside the same statement and therefore the same transaction. Rejected: wrapping each procedure body in START TRANSACTION and COMMIT, which would have reported 0 affected rows and broken every picture write in the application.

The recorded-path move keeps the change record silent through the session flag mtm_picture_layout_move. Reason: the move rewrites every stored image_path and a layout migration is not a picture change, so without the flag one reviewed step would write a change row per stored picture, each naming an actor who never touched it. Rejected: a second UPDATE path with no trigger, which would put two write paths over one table.

IPartPictureResolver is declared with BCL-only signatures and an asynchronous resolve. Reason: MTM_Waitlist.Core references no project, so the contract cannot name PartPictureSystem or any other type this feature adds; asynchronous is what a surface needs because resolution reads the store. Rejected: declaring the interface in MTM_Waitlist.Settings, which would make every surface depend on the picture store.

The shared card binds with Binding rather than x:Bind and declares its own two converter instances inside its own dictionary. Reason: one template serves four lists whose entry models are different types, and a merged dictionary resolves its own StaticResource lookups against the dictionary it sits in, so depending on the application-level converter instances would be a template that cannot be parsed in isolation. Rejected: a shared base model type for the four lists.

RegisterPartPictureServices is a partial method declared once in the composition root and implemented in the feature own file. Reason: that is the pattern the three existing story-phase registrations already use and it keeps each phase registrations in a file that phase owns, at the cost of one declaration and one call in the composition root. Rejected: a static contribution list, which would still need a declaration to make the contribution run.
The storage panel saves the picture folder, the key folder and the retention period with one button, because three buttons over three boxes on one panel is three chances to leave it half saved.

The storage panel reads this machine own configured folder from IOptions<ImageStorageOptions> rather than from the resolver, because the resolver already answers store wins and comparing it with itself would always report agreement.
The picture-cache panel gate moved to permission.settings.storage_paths, and its tests now pin that the widened picture entitlement no longer opens it.

The dunnage type card carries the shared no-image placeholder: the panel's own read returns a type name and identifier and no picture path, and dunnage pictures keep their own storage and arrangement (FR-033), so no dunnage read was widened to invent one

The master lists were rebuilt by slicing each aggregate at its own block headers and re-emitting only the changed and new blocks, so the regeneration is byte-exact and leaves 2000 unrelated lines untouched

The owning view model resolves the picture and the model only carries it: every surface that draws a part takes IPartPictureResolver through constructor injection and assigns the resolved path or the shared placeholder to the model before the model reaches a bound collection, so a card draws a value it was handed. Rejected: resolving inside the model, which would have made plain data read files and know a storage root.

The request's material part is the value the card's own identifier resolves {part_number} from, exposed once from WaitlistRequestTitles and reused by the wizard. Rejected: reusing the Item's configured picture (that is the picture for the kind of request, FR-019) and adding separate die and component arms (more rules than the contract asks for).

A part's local copy sits at the collection's own cache folder plus the recorded path below the collection. The resolver had been prepending the collection to a path that already named it, so no part copy was ever found on this machine and every draw went back to the share. Rejected: leaving the doubled path and widening the cache lookup instead.
The Setup and wizard list models default their picture to ImagePicturePolicy.NoImagePath, so a surface added without a placeholder path fails its own test rather than drawing a blank space.
The owning view model resolves the picture and the model only carries it; rejected resolving inside the model, which would make plain data read files and know a storage root.
The request's material part is the value the card's own identifier resolves part_number from, exposed once from WaitlistRequestTitles; rejected reusing the Item's configured kind-of-request picture.

A part's local copy sits at the collection's own cache folder plus the recorded path below the collection; the resolver had been prepending the collection to a path that already named it, so no local copy was ever found.
The Setup and wizard list models default their picture to the shared placeholder, so a surface added without a placeholder path fails its own test.

The part-picture screen is its own page over the existing override seam, not a derivation of the row-based image-override editor: the screen is one part with a change record and a coverage list, and the row editor's batched-rows base would have been an abstraction with one caller.

The two override services' accepted scopes were widened to visual_part and wip_part, and a store-at-a-layout copy was added to the image storage service. The resolver already reads part rows through that seam, so without the widening a part picture could never be read back and every part drew the placeholder.

The name collision is compared ordinally on the part number and case-insensitively on the file name within the family folder, so a part's own row is a replacement while a number differing only by letter case is a refusal naming the owner.

The missing-picture list composes one part-number source per system. Only the WIP floor can enumerate its parts, so the Visual system is reported in one line as not listable rather than invented, and a Visual part is still picturable by typing its number.
A hand-placed picture resolves by the part's own name when no row records one, looking for each accepted extension on this machine first and then on the share, which is what FR-028 needed.

Each refusal is recorded twice: a sentence in the person's words from the resources, and the code, colliding part and stated limit beside it, so the behaviour can be tested in a host where no resources are loaded.

tasks.summary: Produced 89 tasks in 10 phases and 32 waves: 3 setup, 25 foundational (the store, the layout and its both-layout reader, the recorded-path move, the shared card, and the Settings surfaces three stories share), 12 for US1, 6 for US2, 14 for US3, 3 for US4, 7 for US5, 5 for US6, 7 for US7 and 7 of polish and validation. Each of the 38 requirements is mapped to the tasks that satisfy it.
tasks.key_finding: Three stories need one Settings surface and four lists need one card template, so both are built in the foundational phase: that is the only way to keep every file under one owning phase and still let implement fan out one worker per story.

specify.summary: Built the spine of part pictures: the two part scopes on the existing picture table, one change-record table with its read and its triggers, the dictated share layout with a reader that answers for both layouts, the recorded-path move with its reverse and its paired seed, the part-picture resolver behind a Core contract, the shared card template, and the Settings entry point gated on the widened picture entitlement. 21 of 89 tasks done; the solution builds clean and the suite is green at 1397 passed, 0 failed, 48 skipped.

implement.summary: T071 to T089 reconciled and finished. Two real defects were found and fixed, the solution builds clean, and the full suite is green at 1546 total, 0 failed, 1495 passed, 51 skipped.

approach: Two new scopes on the existing picture table carry one picture per system and part number, with a new history table recording what each change replaced. The share is re-laid-out as one folder per collection and, inside the part collections, one folder per number prefix plus a catch-all, and the reader understands the pre-move layout as well so the move cannot orphan a picture. A part picture is copied to the machine on first draw rather than by the startup mirror, and the picture entitlement widens to Setup Lead and Plant Manager while the storage controls stay on IT Department and Developer.

FR-001.title: Every part the application can name can carry a picture: the Infor Visual parts and the WIP floor parts.

FR-002.title: A Visual part and a WIP part are pictured separately even where they share a part number, and one system's picture is never drawn for the other.

FR-003.title: A part's picture is the same picture wherever that part is named, within its own system.

FR-004.title: A stored picture is kept under the folder for the collection it belongs to: the application's own, the Visual parts, or the WIP parts.

FR-005.title: Within that folder a picture is kept in the folder named for the part's family, and an unrecognised family is kept in the catch-all folder.

FR-006.title: One picture per part per system, its file named after the part.

FR-007.title: Characters a file name cannot hold are replaced, and a replacement colliding with a different part is refused, naming the part it collides with.

FR-008.title: A part number longer than the storage permits is refused when a picture is set, with the limit stated, and never stored truncated.

FR-009.title: The folder holding part pictures is a setting and is not compiled into the application.

FR-010.title: A stored picture is recorded relative to that folder, so the same value resolves under whichever folder a machine is configured with.

FR-011.title: A picture replaced by a later one is kept, and removed once the configured retention period has passed.

FR-012.title: The prefix of a part's number decides the family folder a picture is stored in and read from.

FR-013.title: A part picture is drawn only when the file exists, can be read as a picture, and meets the existing acceptance rule.

FR-014.title: Where a part has no picture, or its picture cannot be drawn, the one shared no-image picture is drawn and never a blank space.

FR-015.title: No category or family artwork may stand in for a part that has no picture.

FR-016.title: The folder holding the key files remains a setting, changeable from the same screen as the picture folder.

FR-017.title: Changing either storage folder remains restricted to the IT Department and Developer roles.

FR-018.title: The Setup part list, the Setup review, the wizard's die card and the wizard's confirmation step each draw the part's picture beside its number.

FR-019.title: The waitlist card draws the part's picture rather than the picture for the kind of request.

FR-020.title: A request whose material cannot be pictured shows the shared placeholder and never the family's picture as a stand-in.

FR-021.title: The lists that ask a person to choose by name present their entries as selectable cards.

FR-022.title: The building choice is a flyout listing every building as a selectable card, without the building currently in effect.

FR-023.title: An entry with no picture is still offered as a card, drawing the shared placeholder.

FR-024.title: A screen sets or replaces one part's picture, offered only to an account holding the picture entitlement.

FR-025.title: The picture entitlement covers IT Department, Developer, Setup Lead and Plant Manager.

FR-026.title: The screen lists the parts that have no picture, and that list is exportable.

FR-027.title: Setting or replacing a picture records who did it, when, and what the previous picture was, and that record is readable.

FR-028.title: A picture placed in the storage folders by hand, named after its part, is used without the application having been used to add it.

FR-029.title: Files the application cannot draw are ignored and are not reported as a fault.

FR-030.title: A part's picture is copied to the computer the first time that part is drawn, rather than all pictures being copied at start.

FR-031.title: A source that cannot be reached is recorded, leaves existing copies in place, and does not prevent a screen from opening.

FR-032.title: An empty source is not treated as evidence that pictures were removed.

FR-033.title: Dunnage pictures are unchanged by this feature, keeping their own storage and arrangement.

FR-034.title: The existing acceptance rule for a picture is not relaxed for part pictures and not tightened for pictures this feature does not touch.

FR-035.title: Every change to stored data ships with its own reversal, and the schema master lists are kept in step.

FR-036.title: Every picture already stored moves under the new arrangement, and every recorded value resolves to its moved file.

FR-037.title: The period a replaced picture is kept before cleanup is a setting, changeable from the same screen, defaulting to ninety days.

FR-038.title: The pictures the application stores for its own screens are kept apart by kind, so no two kinds can resolve to one file.
